answer: Harberger-taxed identity seats: each agent self-assesses a price for its seat and pays a small recurring tax on it into a shared nectar pool that funds jurors. Anyone may buy a seat at its posted price, so a sybil farm must either post low prices and be bought out, or post high ones and bleed tax on every clone. An honest agent keeps one well-valued seat as its haven, while a spammer hits a cost summit long before its fleet can swing a vote.
